summary: Restored piggyback load reporting in the current serving architecture. Scheduler generation and embedding outputs now carry a full LoadSnapshot through detokenization and multi-tokenizer fanout. Each HTTP worker retains the newest per-rank piggyback snapshot, rejects stale out-of-order updates, and merges the cache with the existing watch-mode reader so idle ranks and non-piggybacking schedulers remain queryable through /v1/loads.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: all four tests failed because output snapshots, HTTP-worker caching, timestamp arbitration, and watch/piggyback merging were absent. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ee152f8ccad8/failing-before.log

44 tests and 19 subtests passed, covering best-effort collection, stale-update rejection, watch fallback, timestamp precedence, multi-tokenizer fanout, msgpack round-trip compatibility, and the existing router LoadStat wire contract. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ee152f8ccad8/passing-after.log
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, secret, and CI-registration hooks all passed.

A real source-checkout SGLang server on one AMD Instinct MI355X completed generation, OpenAI completion, batch, streaming, and /v1/loads probes with HTTP 200. The load timestamp and cumulative prefill counters advanced after traffic. Raw server log, requests, responses, and cleanup metadata are retained under /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ee152f8ccad8/serving-evidence.

66 tests passed, but the pre-existing CONFLATE-based TestZmqRoundTrip.test_read_returns_latest intermittently observed snapshot 8 instead of 9. It passed immediately in isolation and is outside the changed piggyback path. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-ee152f8ccad8/focused-tests.log

gpu_evidence: The source checkout served the deterministic tiny Llama on AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950) with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015. Server logs show real prefill/decode execution; /v1/loads reported the MI355X and token capacity 256. GPU utilization and allocated memory returned to zero after cleanup.
remaining_limitations: The deterministic tiny Llama validates HTTP transport and real single-GPU engine execution only; its random weights do not establish model semantic accuracy.
A multi-rank or multi-node deployment was not available, so per-rank piggyback arbitration was covered by unit tests rather than a distributed GPU run.

The optional Rust egress path bypasses the Python detokenizer/tokenizer HTTP-worker loop and therefore does not consume this Python piggyback field; its separate load-query architecture was not modified or validated.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
The unrelated existing ZMQ CONFLATE latest-message test flaked twice in the combined suite by retaining snapshot 8 of 9, then passed in isolation; this change leaves that backend untouched.
